issues.text: One English study found no link once health was allowed for.
issues.problem: Non-significant adjusted HR (0.92, CI 0.78-1.09) written as 'no link'; the unadjusted link existed. Reads as evidence of no effect.
issues.source_says: mortality was higher among ... more lonely participants. However, after adjusting ... loneliness did not [remain associated] (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.78-1.09)
issues.replacement: In one English study, loneliness was no longer linked with death once health at the start was allowed for.

issues.text: Linked with earlier death, less strongly than social isolation. In one English study, no link once health at the start was allowed for. All observational.
issues.problem: Same compression: 'no link' overstates a non-significant adjusted result.
issues.source_says: HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.78-1.09 after adjustment; unadjusted mortality higher in lonely participants
issues.replacement: Linked with earlier death, less strongly than social isolation. In one English study, the link disappeared once health at the start was allowed for. All observational.

issues.text: In one English study there was no link once health at the start was allowed for.
issues.problem: As above.
issues.source_says: HR 0.92 (0.78-1.09) adjusted
issues.replacement: In one English study the link disappeared once health at the start was allowed for.

issues.text: Later reviews of loneliness on its own still find it linked with earlier death, but less strongly than social isolation (having little contact with others).
issues.problem: The 2015 review found loneliness about the same as isolation (OR 1.26 vs 1.29); only the 2023 and 2025 reviews found a smaller link. Also no 'observational' caveat in X.
issues.source_says: Holt-Lunstad 2015: loneliness OR 1.26, isolation 1.29; Wang 2023: 1.14 vs 1.32; Nakou 2025: 1.14 vs 1.35
issues.replacement: The largest recent reviews of loneliness on its own still find it linked with earlier death, but less strongly than social isolation (having little contact with others). These are observational studies.

issues.text: Later reviews still link loneliness with earlier death, but less than social isolation.
issues.problem: As for X: the 2015 review found similar sizes.
issues.source_says: see above
issues.replacement: Recent large reviews still link loneliness with earlier death, but less strongly than social isolation.

issues.text: practice factors, such as how appointments were organised, explained a good part of the pattern.
issues.problem: 'Explained a good part' implies a variance decomposition not reported in the abstract.
issues.source_says: Practice factors also substantially affected attendance patterns
issues.replacement: practice factors, such as how appointments were organised, also made a substantial difference.

issues.text: A discharge letter after two missed appointments treats the absence as a choice.
issues.problem: Specific 'two missed appointments' policy is not in any claim record.
issues.source_says: No source on discharge policies.
issues.replacement: A discharge letter after missed appointments treats the absence as a choice.

issues.text: In Scottish GP records, people over 90 and people in the most deprived areas were among the most likely to miss appointments repeatedly. Missing appointments was linked with higher mortality: a warning sign, not a cause.
issues.problem: Drops the required qualification that young adults were also at higher risk and that the mortality study covered all ages.
issues.source_says: Qualification: mention young adults; mortality study all ages
issues.replacement: In Scottish GP records, people over 90, young adults and people in the most deprived areas were among the most likely to miss appointments repeatedly. In all ages, missing appointments was linked with higher mortality: a warning sign, not a cause.

issues.text: I couldn't get a lift that day.
issues.problem: Invented patient speech. It is labelled 'Illustrative example', but the reason given is not from the studies (which recorded no reasons). Acceptable only if the label stays prominent.
issues.source_says: Studies did not record reasons for non-attendance
issues.replacement: Keep 'Illustrative example' label on the same panel; no wording change needed if label retained.

issues.text: Anxiety eased too. Whether it lasts is unknown.
issues.problem: Compression drops that the second loneliness scale showed no clear difference, making the short version stronger than the others.
issues.source_says: De Jong improvement 0.32 (95% CI -0.20 to 0.81; P=.06)
issues.replacement: Anxiety eased too. A second loneliness scale showed no clear difference, and whether it lasts is unknown.

issues.text: Sixteen students aged 17 to 23
issues.problem: Not all were students: 14 undergraduates, 1 entering community college, 1 graduate student.
issues.source_says: Sixteen people from ages 17 to 23 years, including 14 college undergraduates, 1 person entering community college, and 1 graduate student
issues.replacement: Sixteen young people aged 17 to 23, mostly students

issues.text: Sixteen students aged 17 to 23
issues.problem: As for X.
issues.source_says: as above
issues.replacement: Sixteen young people aged 17 to 23, mostly students

issues.text: The partner at home should be offered their own conversation.
issues.problem: Recommendation not marked as judgement, and the Threads version drops the qualifications that support after a move is untested and that the study is US, 1996-2000, dementia carers.
issues.source_says: C17-07-b qualification: must be written as a judgement, not a proven intervention
issues.replacement: This US study is from 1996 to 2000, and support after a move has barely been tested. Still, I think the partner at home should be offered their own conversation.

issues.text: Support after a move has barely been tested in trials.
issues.problem: Slightly vague; the review found few small trials without clear effect.
issues.source_says: Four studies; no overall effect on burden or depression; very low grade evidence
issues.replacement: Only a few small trials have tested support after a move, without clear effects.

issues.text: 5. A daily visitor or call: contact with others was protective
issues.problem: Attributes a protective finding to daily visits or calls, which neither study measured. Chicago measured social contacts such as group activities or friends in the area. This presents an untested intervention as a finding.
issues.source_says: Having social contacts such as group activities or friends in the area was protective.
issues.replacement: 5. Friends nearby or group activities: linked with lower risk in Chicago

issues.text: light clothes, cooling and contact with others with survival.
issues.problem: Consistent with the fix above; retain but match the measured exposure.
issues.source_says: social contacts such as group activities or friends in the area
issues.replacement: light clothes, cooling, and having friends nearby or group activities with survival.

issues.text: In past heatwaves, older people who were confined to bed, rarely left home, lived alone or slept on a top floor were more likely to die.
issues.problem: Population swap: the Chicago study was of all ages (matched on age), not older people only; only the French study was restricted to people aged 65 and over.
issues.source_says: Chicago: 339 cases and 339 controls matched by neighbourhood and age; France: elderly people living at home
issues.replacement: In the Chicago (1995) and French (2003) heatwaves, people who were confined to bed, rarely left home, lived alone or slept on a top floor were more likely to die.

issues.text: The financial gain is well supported.
issues.problem: Overstates certainty: the review said all studies reported financial gain but the studies were generally of poor quality and care must be taken in drawing firm conclusions.
issues.source_says: given the generally poor scientific quality of the studies, care must be taken in drawing firm conclusions
issues.replacement: The financial gain was reported consistently, though by mostly weak studies.

issues.text: Well supported: people ended up better off financially (all 14 studies)
issues.problem: Same overstatement on the visual; column heading 'Well supported' also.
issues.source_says: as above
issues.replacement: Consistently reported: people ended up better off financially (all 14 studies)

issues.text: Well supported
issues.problem: Column heading overstates certainty.
issues.source_says: as above
issues.replacement: Consistently reported

issues.text: Well supported: people ended up better off financially in all 14.
issues.problem: Match visual fix.
issues.source_says: as above
issues.replacement: Consistently reported: people ended up better off financially in all 14.

issues.text: The authors warned that their generally poor quality means firm conclusions should not be drawn.
issues.problem: Slightly stronger than source.
issues.source_says: care must be taken in drawing firm conclusions
issues.replacement: The authors warned that, given the generally poor quality of the studies, care must be taken in drawing firm conclusions.

issues.text: Sexual activity at 75 to 85 is common
issues.problem: 26 in 100 described as 'common'; qualification says use natural frequencies rather than vague quantifiers.
issues.source_says: 26% among respondents 75 to 85
issues.replacement: About 1 in 4 people aged 75 to 85 are sexually active

issues.text: Few had discussed sex with a doctor.
issues.problem: 38% of men is not 'few'; and 'in the past year' missing from activity figure.
issues.source_says: 38% of men and 22% of women reported having discussed sex with a physician since the age of 50
issues.replacement: Only about 4 in 10 men and 1 in 5 women had discussed sex with a doctor since 50.

issues.text: in one trial, only chlorthalidone clearly differed from placebo.
issues.problem: The difference was at 24 months only, in people aged 45 to 69; by 48 months it was not significant.
issues.source_says: chlorthalidone 17.1% vs placebo 8.1% through 24 months; through 48 months nonsignificant differences
issues.replacement: in one trial of five blood pressure medicines, only chlorthalidone clearly differed from placebo, and only over the first 2 years.
